column1: Number of Islands — given m×n grid of '1' (land) and '0' (water), return the count of islands. An island is a maximal 4-directionally connected group of '1's. Example: grid with three connected components of land → 3.
column2: PATTERN: DFS / BFS flood fill. | INSIGHT: Each unvisited '1' starts a flood fill that marks the whole island. | STEPS: 1) count=0. 2) For each cell: if grid[r][c]=='1': count+=1; dfs(r,c). 3) dfs(r,c): bounds + check '1'; set to '0'; recurse to 4 neighbors. 4) Return count. | TIME/SPACE: O(m·n) / O(m·n) recursion in worst case. | PITFALL: Mutating the grid is allowed and saves a visited set.

column1: Surrounded Regions — given m×n board of 'X' and 'O'; flip every 'O' region completely surrounded by 'X' to 'X'. Border-touching 'O' regions stay. Example: only inner 'O' regions get captured.
column2: PATTERN: Reverse approach — mark border-connected 'O's as safe first. | INSIGHT: A region is captured iff none of its cells touch the border. Easier to find border-connected ones than to test surroundedness. | STEPS: 1) For each border cell: if 'O': dfs marking 'S' (safe). 2) Final pass: if 'O' → 'X'; if 'S' → 'O'. | TIME/SPACE: O(m·n) / O(m·n). | PITFALL: Don't try to detect surrounded regions directly — work backwards from borders.

column1: Clone Graph — given a reference to a node in a connected undirected graph, return a deep copy. Each node has val and neighbors list. Example: node with neighbors [2,4]; cloned graph mirrors structure exactly.
column2: PATTERN: DFS / BFS with hashmap orig→clone. | INSIGHT: Map original→clone; recurse on neighbors; reuse map entries on cycles. | STEPS: 1) m={}. 2) clone(node): if not node: None. If node in m: return m[node]. m[node]=Node(node.val). For nb in node.neighbors: m[node].neighbors.append(clone(nb)). Return m[node]. | TIME/SPACE: O(V+E) / O(V). | PITFALL: Insert into the map BEFORE recursing on neighbors to handle cycles.

column1: Evaluate Division — given equations like a/b=k.0 (as string pairs and value array) and queries c/d, evaluate each query (or -1.0 if any variable unknown / unreachable). Example: equations=[['a','b'],['b','c']], values=[2.0,3.0], queries=[['a','c'],['b','a'],['x','x']] → [6.0, 0.5, -1.0].
column2: PATTERN: Build weighted graph + DFS multiplying edge weights. | INSIGHT: a/b=k → directed edges a→b weight k and b→a weight 1/k. Query c/d = product of weights along any path c→d. | STEPS: 1) Build adjacency: g[a][b]=k, g[b][a]=1/k. 2) For each query (c,d): if c not in g or d not in g: -1.0. Else DFS from c looking for d, accumulating product (visited set to avoid cycles). | TIME/SPACE: O(E + Q·V) / O(V). | PITFALL: Union-find with weights is the alternate, faster approach for many queries.

column1: Course Schedule — n courses labeled 0..n-1 with prerequisite pairs [a,b] meaning b must precede a; return True if you can finish all courses. Example: 2, prereqs=[[1,0]] → True; [[1,0],[0,1]] → False.
column2: PATTERN: Cycle detection in directed graph (DFS with 3 colors). | INSIGHT: A cycle means impossible. White=unvisited, gray=in progress, black=done; seeing a gray during DFS = back edge = cycle. | STEPS: 1) Build adj list. 2) state=[0]*n. 3) dfs(u): if state[u]==1: return True (cycle). If state[u]==2: return False. state[u]=1; for v in adj[u]: if dfs(v): return True. state[u]=2; return False. 4) For all u: if dfs(u): return False. Return True. | TIME/SPACE: O(V+E) / O(V+E). | PITFALL: Kahn's BFS topo sort is the alternate — count nodes processed.

column1: Course Schedule II — same setup; return any valid topological order, or [] if impossible. Example: 4 courses, prereqs=[[1,0],[2,0],[3,1],[3,2]] → [0,2,1,3] (one valid order).
column2: PATTERN: Kahn's algorithm (BFS topological sort). | INSIGHT: Repeatedly process nodes with in-degree 0; decrement neighbors' in-degree. | STEPS: 1) Build adj list and in_degree. 2) q=deque([nodes with indeg 0]). 3) ans=[]; while q: u=q.popleft(); ans.append(u); for v in adj[u]: indeg[v]-=1; if indeg[v]==0: q.append(v). 4) Return ans if len(ans)==n else []. | TIME/SPACE: O(V+E) / O(V+E). | PITFALL: If final ans length != n, there's a cycle — return [].
